findings.message: The record now carries a per-file snapshot (`files`), yet this file's line 44 still says nothing here stores new mutable state except the merge receipt, and line 37's formula iterates files 'changed since record.digest' as if a digest enumerated them. The preamble the diff adds names the deleted contracts but not this deviation from R-9's own design.
findings.minimal_fix: Add one preamble sentence: R-9's record stores the review-scope content keys (not per-lens scope) so staleness is answerable per file.

findings.message: The first-round dispatch still iterates `plan.lenses` while the refine loop uses `replan.run`; on a resumed run with fresh records every lens is dispatched again, contradicting the review skill's 'a lens whose record still describes the change is not dispatched again'.
findings.minimal_fix: Dispatch `plan.run || plan.lenses` in the first round too.

findings.message: The preamble lists R-1, R-2, R-3, R-5, R-6, R-7, R-8 and R-16 as struck; spec.md:41 also strikes R-4 (deleted, ADR-5). The list is inaccurate by that omission.
findings.minimal_fix: Insert R-4 into the struck list.

findings.message: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:321 and :364 say a change to answers.json/waivers.json re-takes every review; that is true only if correctness F-2 is fixed in code. If F-2 is instead resolved by amending the requirement, these lines must move with it (file not in the lease).
findings.minimal_fix: Fix F-2 in `lens_staleness`; otherwise reword both lines to 're-takes the always-on lens'.

findings.message: README says a review is invalidated by 'an edit afterwards' (lines 116 and 223); after R-9 only the lenses the moved files' kinds select are. Not in the lease — named for the follow-up.
findings.minimal_fix: 'an edit afterwards to a file whose kinds select that lens invalidates it'.
